notes.title: Improved movement mechanics, pressure plate overhaul and more
notes.content: [p]Hi everyone,[/p][p]It has already been almost 5 months since the release of Invertigo. We are so happy to see people enjoying the game (and battle each other for the speed running records). We are back with another update to Invertigo with some big changes such as an overhaul of the pressure plates and improvements to the movement mechanics. We hope you enjoy![/p][p][/p][p]Full change log including hotfix[/p][list][*][p]The pressure plate mechanics have been overhauled to fix the pressure plate jank for once and for all and make their behaviour more predictable. [/p][/*][*][p]Parkour mechanics have been improved with the implementation of Coyote time, allowing the player to jump shortly after running off a platform.[/p][/*][*][p]Other small tweaks to player movement code, largely related to grounding and standing still on slopes or mantling.[/p][/*][*][p]Added button to clear all progress.[/p][/*][*][p]Added V-sync toggle.[/p][/*][*][p]Mouse jitter has been reduced.[/p][/*][*][p]The framerate is now unlocked instead of capped at 240 fps.[/p][/*][*][p]Fix janky mantling mechanic while gravity switching.[/p][/*][*][p]Fix the bug that causes the credits to play while loading another level after finishing the final level.[/p][/*][*][p]Fix a bunch of out-of-bounds bugs and janky collisions in Recreational Area, Water Management and Emergency Storage.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved performance while standing on movers.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed bug where scoreboard did not function properly if two people had the same steam name. [/p][/*][*][p]Improved performance in Reactor and Water Management.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a severe performance bug involving movers, mostly noticeable with the elevator in the first level.[/p][/*][*][p]Use IL2CPP for building the project, should result in slightly improved performance in some cases.[/p][/*][*][p]Switch to forward renderer instead of deferred.[/p][/*][*][p]Enable dynamic resolution for all quality levels.[/p][/*][*][p]Enable MSAA anti-aliasing for all quality levels.[/p][/*][*][p]Gravity shift camera is now properly untied from the FPS[/p][/*][*][p]Gravity shift camera stabilization can be configured with a slider in the input tab[/p][/*][*][p]Minimized mouse overshooting upper and lower bounds, for those fast flicks[/p][/*][*][p]Added FPS limit slider in options[/p][/*][*][p]Updated to new InputSystem version, which means:[/p][/*][*][p]You can now bind scroll up/down to anything![/p][/*][*][p]Binding 'E' wasn't working before, it works now, so you can play with ESDF :)[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed level transition flash sometimes being missing[/p][/*][*][p]Use 'Medium' quality preset as default[/p][/*][*][p]Restart Level can now be bound to a key[/p][/*][*][p]Fix music retriggering when entering and leaving airlock[/p][/*][*][p]The spawn limit of the cans in Coffee Break and Recreational Area has been increased. We won't reveal how high it is now...[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/6381b5b5c9a55f94d6898ed4a3ecd0e4d767d4bd.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Post-release fixes
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We've brought out a new update, mostly just fixes all around. The biggest thing is probably that Steam Deck players should finally be able to play it as well, since that didn't work due to some broken resolution settings and an options menu that didn't function as a result. Have fun!

Change log:
- Fix resolution loading/initialization problem on non 1080p screens that could crash the options menu
- Properly unlink the link mode when disconnected via mover
- Fix typo in "Ophelia - 8" datalog
- Make tutorial overlay texts not cut off for longer bind names
- Add shorthand for middle mouse button for HUD
- Fix some more reflection probe ranges on Coffee Break
- Add reflection probe to exit airlock of Emergency Storage
- Fix some collision issues on Emergency Storage room
- Patch visible hole on Equipment Bay
- Fix reflection probes on Equipment Bay
- Fix tiny airlock gap on Server Room
- Fix high score notice not showing in the level complete text
- Fix missing x-ray arrows for pressure plates on Server Room
- Fix missing collision for wall on Big Vent
- Fix Coffee Break door not becoming red after closing
- Make goop on Emergency Storage more blue
- Fix buggy pillar collision on Water Management

notes.title: Invertigo official release
notes.content:
We're thrilled to announce that Invertigo has now been officially released. We hope you'll have a great time with the game, it was definitely a special journey for us to make it and we can't wait to hear what you think, so don't forget to leave a review or reach us through the discord. 

There is now a 20% release discount of Invertigo as a thank you to everyone who has supported us throughout the years.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/dae28bf748cbc66c7beb71e25499bd9d6415959c.jpg[/img]

notes.title: New demo release for Invertigo
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

We have released an updated version of the demo of Invertigo today. Play it through Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1659520/Invertigo/

The new demo has a bunch of new functionalities and bugfixes. For example, you don't have to switch between the gravity modules anymore to use them. You can now use the gravity shift with the left mouse button and the gravity link with the right mouse button. 'E' can be used for the gravity hold module. Furthermore, the aforementioned controller support has been implemented. You can seamlessly switch between mouse and keyboard and controller while playing.

Other UI updates include an overhaul of the pause menu. The menu now contains both the scoreboard and the lore menu. The level select screen has also been reworked and is now also included on the main menu. The settings have been updated as well with for example a new 'invert mouse' option and an FOV slider.

And, as we showed in the last announcement, the game now starts with a level that combines the fan-favourite level Coffee Break with the mysterious room from the announcement. Because of this the old demo scoreboard for coffee break has to be wiped since that level no longer exists. Don't worry, the scoreboards for all the other levels will stay as they are :). To celebrate our original heroes who performed speedruns in the old coffee break, the top 100 hall of fame of that scoreboard will be posted in the high score channel of the discord to be immortalized. You can also see this top 100 here below.

So have fun playing the new demo! We're always happy to receive feedback to make Invertigo better, so let us know what you think.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/cc139a2dbeb7f94f4c815f74018fe22503df985e.png[/img]

Demo release changelog
- Removed gravity module switching, instead they can be invoked directly if available
- Added full gamepad support, with seamless switching
- Updated coffee break to have the official start of the game, along with new voice lines
- Added FOV slider
- Added invert mouse toggle
- Overhauled level selection menu
- Added save data (demo begins with all levels unlocked, but it will save anomaly/datalog collection)
- Added level select to main menu
- Added scoreboard and lore menu buttons to pause menu
- Gun screen now only gives visual feedback if the link module is enabled, and on picking up new modules
- Graphics presets actually work now

First of all, we can finally share our vision of the start of the game with you. I could explain it all, but I think images say a lot more so here's a gif.

After that, there is a seamless transition to the original 'coffee break' level with a hallway, decorated with all kinds of plants.

notes.title: Server room, air cleaning, reactor updates and new technical functionalities
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

It's been a while but we have a lot of progress we'd like to share with you. Firstly, a major overhaul has been made to the server room level to make the puzzle more enjoyable: platforms are now wider to prevent you from falling off of them and some alternatives routes/methods have been added to make the level more interesting to both speedrunners and casual players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/456aff074bae955abc38ced701413d72f8134dd5.png[/img]

We have also been working on new levels, such as the level 'air cleaning'. A tiny triangular level with a surprisingly tricky puzzle. You can see the current status of this level below. Besides this, we are continuously working on polishing our existing levels such as the reactor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/d8ddf0c8043958314ceb8def7fea02a7b370d4f2.png[/img]

Level design isn't the only progress we'd like to talk about. On the more technical side of things, an FOV slider has been added with a default setting of 90 degrees. But below you can also see examples for an FOV of 60 and 150 degrees. Other functionalities we're working on are an achievement and a save system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/f766096beb41a2520cbc02aa1e71315f40a71d02.png[/img]

notes.title: Bugfixing scoreboard, updates to camera and more
notes.content:
First of all happy new year! It's been a while, but we have been working hard on Invertigo and are very excited to share some of the progress we have made since the last announcement. First of all, as of just now there is an updated version of the Invertigo demo on Steam as of now. This demo contains two main updates:

*Fixed the erroneous scoreboard high-score overwriting. Also, there is no lag spike anymore when starting a new level.
*The new default settings have a new gravity shift camera and a ring beneath your character that indicates the ground. You can see the ring in the image below. These changes have been made to reduce motion sickness and orientation issues. For people who don't want the ring and want the legacy gravity shift camera this can be toggled in the settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/88369c3056e031322121e0777f24eca257e96a7b.png[/img]

Besides these fixes we've also worked on new levels. One level we'd like to showcase is the reactor. Critical to make sure that the other levels still get the required power and supplies, the player has to fix the reactor in this mind-bending level which makes use of walkways and of course gravity in a lot of different directions. Here's a preview of the puzzle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/fbb66ab3d50d23185eadc0c10e3ce1c00bfa0ff0.png[/img]

Finally, some other minor bugfixes/improvements:
*Some binds got renamed
*More visible checkmarks in the options menu
*Scoreboard now centers on you by default, and loads slightly faster
*Fixes for captions/dialogue/ground-ring toggles not working immediately across levels

notes.title: Recreational room and industrial corridors
notes.content:
Firstly we want to give a warm welcome to all our recent new arrivals in the discord and on our Steam wishlist. We can't put into words how exciting it is to see our discord grow and to see people enjoy our game. So a big thank you to Creem for streaming our game and bringing it to a larger audience.

The last few weeks we've been very busy with some of the levels for the full game so in this announcement we'd like to give a preview of some of our progress. One of the levels in current development is the recreational room. Tired of all the puzzling? Take a seat and stare at the beautiful palm trees while enjoying your 15 minutes of relaxation. Furthermore, we'd like to show some early progress on a level called 'industrial corridors'. Some screenshots of the early blockout of this level are shown below. The industrial corridors run through the maintenance area of the station and can be used by the player to get to different areas of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/7f8455fdf19b84f06aa014fc374113a4e32fea8d.png[/img]

To give you an idea of the direction we want to go with the industrial corridors I also attached some concept art here. Once again thanks everyone for being active in the discord and for playing our game. We'll continue to keep you up to date regularly with these sort of progress updates.

notes.title: Invertigo Update: improved gravity shifts and scoreboard
notes.content:
While we are still working hard on the full version of the game, we thought we could already provide you with some fixes and new features with an update of the demo. You can update the free demo of Invertigo on Steam as of today. This update contains the following fixes and features.

Improved gravity shifts
*The view tries to level with the floor now
*A speed curve is used to reduce motion sickness
*Gravity shifts in general are faster and smoother

Improved scoreboard
*Developer scores can be toggled on, which means you can also compete with our times if you want
*The histogram to look at the distribution of results from the community has been improved
*Steam avatars and as well as Steam friend icons are now included
*The scoreboard is now also scrollable

And one more thing: the gravity tool can now only be used after you open the door of the airlock. The era of speedrunning while doing all your moves inside the airlock is over.

notes.title: Cold storage level
notes.content:
Today we want to highlight the progress on one of our new puzzles called 'cold storage'. The process of going from an idea to a fully-fledged level consists of many steps. We start with a brainstorm about the purpose of the level within the story. This results in a sketch with a basic design of the puzzle. Afterwards a first blockout of the level is made in Unity. This is then used to make concept art to better flesh out the look and details of the level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/311934f849c42f213222c1157e8ff78ea696227c.png[/img]

After the concept art more details are added until we are happy with the end result. And we are very pleased with our final version of the cold storage level, which you can see below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/eec71f395ff51967890b8596061af5852e8541f7.png[/img]

notes.title: Vent control, server room, demo details
notes.content:
In recent weeks we've continued polishing the levels that will be included in the demo. One of these is vent control, which we briefly showed in the last announcement. Since then it received an extensive rework as well as added details by means of decals and lights. See the current state of the level below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/d4ed19a8d6175e9b24beb33edd467a5808f52c79.png[/img]

Another level we can't wait to show you is the server room, which will allow you to parkour in many unique ways. Can you best the most efficient path?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/01b5f4a532088195e0c4429a44b614c7733056af.png[/img]

Other levels have also been updated such as the coffee break level, which now has a secret room. We're interested to hear how many of you will manage to find this hidden place once the demo releases. The images below are in-game footage of this new room as well as other minor updates to levels such as the pantry and intersection levels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/e2d04e489e7047fb8c5c0cde46fbb5bb0314bab8.png[/img]

Now that the demo is coming closer we can give you some more details about it. The demo will contain 6 fully worked out levels of the game to give you an idea of what to expect with the full version. This new demo will also have full steam integration with leaderboards so you can test your speedrunning skills. Our goal is to release the demo in early December. We'll let you know when we have a more precise release date.

notes.title: Level design, UI updates, and technical fixes
notes.content:
Since the last announcement we've continued working on level design, UI updates, and technical fixes. A few of the new levels that we've been working on are called vent control and a new parkour level and can be seen below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/1b91e48412d9b43d3edd3ce17b714fb77f2d795a.png[/img]

Part of the recent progress also concerns updates to already existing levels such as food processing and greenhouse. This includes more extensive artwork and details such as dirt patches. The levels also contain more interactable items such as lights and effects that only activate once the puzzle is solved. These levels are now in the final stages of completion in preparation for a new official demo for Invertigo that we'll release soon. More about that in the upcoming announcement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/84279138299ac44e5d4377cfd0af27d3a7cee9e8.png[/img]

In preparation for the demo a lot of time was spent to solve bugs and to improve UI elements. This includes mantling and movement issues such as getting stuck on ledges, gravity tool errors, glitching blocks and more. Another big update regards the data log framework. The data logs, story elements which can be collected throughout the level, are now stored in a separate UI system as shown below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/4d34aeb4a9aeeb2d67e9b683df246265146ac918.png[/img]

Finally, a new speedrunning system has been introduced including a leaderboard which can be accessed from within the game. Both the time as well as the number of gravity moves are saved. This not only allows you to look up your own personal best stats, but also makes it possible to compare them with other players as you can see here (player names have been removed from this screenshot).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/2e9296293975c3f79200e3455e3b1a67c58c4cc2.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
Since our last announcement we've continued to work on the detailed design of multiple of our total of 25 levels. Two levels which we'd like to share with you are called 'coffee break' and 'equipment bay'. Coffee break is one of the earliest levels in the game as is intended as a place for staff on the station to relax. It is connected to a lot of other elements of the ship and as such it has a maze-like aesthetic to it. Here below are a few screenshots of the level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/84a4276aac67484fb6d4f70532879638ed6878cf.jpg[/img]

The second level comes along quite a bit later into the game and is called the equipment bay. As the name suggests it is used to store parts of the station and contains tools to fix any damage to the facility.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/d0c7e59961a6178346993d5989d3e95d72b909cd.png[/img]

Finally, we'd like to mention a few technical fixes and developments. The movement-related mechanics have received a full overhaul to make it feel more natural and to fix issues such as the ability to slide over steep slopes. Similarly, the gravity tool mechanics have been updated. One example is the gravity plane change move, which used to position the player slightly to the side of where they wanted to go. However, with these fixes this problem has been resolved.

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
In the previous announcement we mentioned our progress on the greenhouse level. Since then we've decorated the level with a lot of plants, flowers, and other assets to make it look like an actual greenhouse. This is the first time that we've used these foliage models in-game so let us know what you think.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/4b2ae5fb69ae6e89c7fd3b7ea50ea588cb4cc9fa.png[/img]

We now also have a lot of decals, small details which can be added to assets and which we can use to make the levels feel more unique and lively. Below is an example of an asset with decals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/eea6c9d5d81d84ddf244fdba94307eb794c30a7a.png[/img]

Finally, we've also been working on another level called 'water management'. You might've seen some early concept art for it in an announcement a few months ago, but now we have an actual blockout.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/1bec28d2922ed47a6216e4f8fadc4e679080a9ce.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
Since our last announcement we've been working on new assets and functionalities which we've directly implemented into the greenhouse level, a level which you might've already seen a few times in previous announcements. We'll go over the updates one by one. Firstly, we now have six new differently sized wall panels which allow for a much more varied aesthetic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/27749721aa6f9885a713277662dd25162662ed4b.png[/img]

The greenhouse level in general has been updated significantly with new assets and updated lighting. The plants still need to be added, but the level is very close to being done.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/3e565126160eefecd044e0a07c6731779fc0c521.png[/img]

When you play the eventual version of the game, be on the lookout for any easter eggs or hidden rooms. We already mentioned the data logs which can be found in each level, but there's also for example this secret room.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/de9f241d75c00ec736e03441bf7a5ae893d27858.png[/img]

Finally, a lot of new pillar models have been made which can be used as support structures or platforms from which to jump to other parts of the level. The big vent level from a few announcements ago will for example make use of these.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/959c555d9356b9b55450dcc1011d3a3bdf069123.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
It's been a while since the last announcement and we've made a lot of progress since then that we'd like to share with you. Firstly, we've been working on some new levels. One of these is currently known as the 'pantry level'. A blockout with basic lighting has been made, which you can see below. The level starts in a reddish industrial area and eventually ends with a puzzle based on the concept art from the previous announcement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/221fe381902a0342560cb5a5b6466f26f19fde55.png[/img]

Secondly, the pillars shown in the previous announcement have now been implemented and can extend based on triggers in the level such as pressure plates or timers. The pillars themselves have also received slight upgrades to their design and panels have been made to surround and encase the pillars.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/c8e9b3dee3002b58b096f8c15261513f184c9b35.gif[/img]

Finally, the game now also supports triggerable force fields. These can for example be used to activate a stream of particles with a lever as can be seen below. These particles can also induce a force to push the player into a specific direction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/2ac789fdd966dbc49635696e7b492a7d97e144a6.gif[/img]

notes.title: Progress update
notes.content:
We've continued working on Invertigo the last few weeks and here's some of our progress. Firstly, we've made a few more assets for the game. This includes foliage models for the greenhouse level. You can see some of the new plants models below. We've also expanded tweaked the pillar models and added versions with broken glass.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/debcc29eaf797f95d90959b7a00f2ca5c1742cc7.png[/img]

Secondly, we also have some new concept art to share. Specifically, we've been working on concept art for the pantry/kitchen level. The eventual version of the level will contain conveyor belts and many different food items, but even without that the current concept art should already give you a good idea of the kind of gravity bending puzzles we want to implement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/75aca89e4bfa78cdc3d6b24ae5fe8b7cf3cdba68.png[/img]

Thirdly, we'd like to mention a few other additions and bug fixes. The system to implement data logs into the game, shown with the concept art a few announcements ago, has now been implemented into the game. The data logs can be accessed by interacting with control panels throughout the levels. Furthermore, we've fixed the bug that caused batteries and other objects to glitch through the walls of the level and disappear. A bug that prevented players from jumping when standing on the edge of a platform has also been resolved.

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
Here's an overview of our work on Invertigo since the last announcement. Firstly, we're very happy to tell you that we've now completed the block-out of level 3, the large storage room. You can see some screenshots of the level below. The only things we still need to add are a few story-related elements, material textures, and VFX such as fog particles. But in principle the level is now playable from beginning to end with our intended final assets. Let us know what you think.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/c1b412b3845cef3199c524bebbf91b0bbab59397.jpg[/img]

We've also been working on new assets that will be needed for some of the upcoming levels. This includes new see-through pillars which you can see below. The spawn airlock has also been upgraded with improved lighting and a redesign of the model to fit better with the rest of our assets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/d299c19d685199d99166dbcf6e0690a1c44d4a22.png[/img]

Furthermore, we've also started work on a new level. This level is called 'big vent' as its working title and will require the player to interact with moving pillars and also to use the fan mechanics in order to get to the exit door. You can see a Blender model and early block-out of the level below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/472803d1407bf8041646d0eea1092999c18d19d9.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
To dress up the physical levels, we've been working on designing new modular elements such as panels and pipes. Here's an overview of some of these new elements as well as an implementation of the new pipes to the right in level 3.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/f7db2b01e2cf4a87d05ce65f1bf683d4edccc2b7.png[/img]

Of course an announcement wouldn't be an announcement without new concept art. Here's a sketch for one of the, later levels in the game. We specifically used this one to test some of the new modular elements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/4c643b7a2b85c979c143a6f7c9d551668be9356b.png[/img]

Finally, we'd like to show something completely different. For quite some time we've been working on the storyline for the game. We've now finished the basic outline of the plot and have started working on a more detailed script. One of the ways to communicate the story to the player will be by means of data logs that can be found throughout the levels. Here's a prototype version of one of these data logs for level 1. It's a short interview with Norman, the mysterious leader of the all-powerful Norman Corporation with some very questionable motives. We made the logs with two different backgrounds so let us know which one you prefer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/30e5d517d16644f4bab28f0f0256c6b73d4b6d28.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
On behalf of the Invertigo development team, a happy new year to all of you. In the last few weeks we've enjoyed our nice winter holiday (we hope you did too) and now we're back and ready to continue working on Invertigo. Here I'd like to share some of our progress of the past weeks. Firstly, we've continued working on new concept art. This ranges from a rough schematic overview of the puzzle (left image) to fullly fledged artwork (right image).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/9d7bc7013621725da1ec9f78310e44ffd70e7517.png[/img]

Some artwork assets have now also been implemented in the game. One example of this is a new door model. The image below shows the old door model to the right and the new model on the left.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/c6853dbd3285ae0b4554ffd5fd49eb2e7e17dcbd.png[/img]

Finally, we wanted to show you the progress we've made on the remake of level 3 since our last announcement. We have a lot of exciting things that we're working on and can't wait to show them to you so stay tuned for our next announcement later this month.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/720b85f3a7454724933f92df3c944057759ea9d9.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
The last few weeks we've spent a lot of time making new levels and redesigning already existing rooms. One of these updated levels is an elevator shaft, of which a blockout can be seen below. In this level the elevator will not only be relevant for transport, but also to solve the puzzle itself. Note that this level is still a work-in-progress and that the art style will still be refined and updated over the next few weeks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/e7c29cb0d6be503283e5f372bba07560bfd5366c.jpg[/img]

Furthermore, we'd like to give an update on some of the tutorial levels that we already showed in the last announcement. They've been updated with new assets and we've been experimenting with some new lighting settings. Below you can see two examples. They still need some tweaking, but let us know what you think.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/b72865c8d35c3431808ec28cf7f285d0f4116fb8.png[/img]

Finally, the emergency storage room (level 1 in the demo of Invertigo) has also being redesigned. While we're still in the progress of blocking out this level, we can already give you a preview of its new layout.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/8977295c451888edc5770bb7cc1e848e9cbb191b.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
We wanted to keep you up to date on our latest progress, so here's another announcement with exciting developments that we want to share with you. Firstly, we'd like to show you detailed blender models and sketches of some of the items that you might have already seen in the previous screenshots of level 1. Below you can see a new bench model, as well as concept art as a blender model for the life support pod from which the player wakes up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/4919aa2c8e59fe8010d1fe059df36f8e2f723faf.png[/img]

We've also been working on other artwork related assets. The gravity stations, where the player can get the different modes of the gravity tool, have been redesigned and now look more like glowing disks on the floor as you can see here. You can also see some possible redesigns for other items such as elevator panels and the batteries (red blocks).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/4a9e3abd055cdad8e9183635b71708fd980430ff.png[/img]

Finally, we've been working on a lot of extra levels. Some of the feedback we received is that there is a steep learning curve regarding the gravity tool modes at the start of the game and therefore we're busy adding multiple easier tutorial-like levels so the player can get acquainted with the new mechanics. Here you can see a few screenshots of those levels in different stages of completion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/c6e69625914eb8002a87970d9958b0dff8f18a7a.png[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
It's been a while since our last update, but since then we've made a lot of exciting progress that we can't wait to share with you. Firstly, we worked on the very first level of the game, a level that does not yet exist in the demo. This is the room in which the player wakes up from a cocoon-like life support tank. Here's a snapshot of the current version of the level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/08dcbe3f2fe21f971700494970d4c6338ef253be.png[/img]

We're still continuing to work on this level and have some cool concept art to share with you about our idea of the eventual version of the level. Check out this artwork for the room where the player wakes up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/d142b6e167f21d486f78f3912174c1d2113c8edf.jpg[/img]

As well as this concept art for the so-called 'decontamination tunnel'. The current state of the tunnel can be seen in the left image.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/2a585e27fe2c0c7cfb7bd092a0286a8782c14b11.png[/img]

Finally, there are some bug fixes that we want to mention. There has been an upgrade to pressure plates which now prevents the plate element from going through walls or from getting stuck. Furthermore, in the current demo the grab tool sometimes rotates and accelerates blocks in an unexpected manner, causing them to 'jump' when released. This especially happened if you moved the block rapidly. As you can see in the gif below, this has now been fixed. So no more flying battery blocks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/cef1c130916608d9735d1b4574e9f940ed7c3855.gif[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
During the past weeks we've been hard at work to create new levels for Invertigo. Firstly, here's the design for a new level named Equipment Bay:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/19161090c2cd991ff9fd3922a33f6bbf7f45ef73.png[/img]

Here's a sneak preview of a new level we've been working on!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/634114205806be7dd08a8264e53931a6ade21f14.png[/img]

And finally, here is a preview of our 'mover' feature in our latest level named 'garbage disposal'. These garbage chutes can change to another position when certain pressure plates are activated. These movers will be used to create many more interesting puzzles!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/1f08df4aa5f0f491b55d29a9a03e60fea882b33a.gif[/img]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
Past week, we've upgraded our movers a bit. They can do cool tricks now, such chaining onto each other, rotating, and triggering other things. Check it out in this cool GIF!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40683812/a4d81b2877ae3d31a63a0ad273c03510af1b98dc.gif[/img]

We've also finished the block-out for a new level, can you guess what kind of environment it will be? (HINT: it looks like trash now... but it will also after!)
